newsitem.title: SYRIA: Sudan leaders in Syria on Arab tour about fighting.
newsitem.headline: Sudan leaders in Syria on Arab tour about fighting.

text.p: Sudanese Vice-President al-Zubeir Mohammad Saleh arrived in Damascus on Monday as part of a tour to brief Arab leaders on the conflict in Sudan, officials and diplomats said.
Saleh and Foreign Minister Ali Osman Mohammad Taha were greeted on arrival at the airport from Saudi Arabia by Syrian Vice-President Abdel-Halim Khaddam and Foreign Minister Farouq al-Shara.
The Sudanese military government has called for mobilisation against what it says are attacks by troops of neighbours Eritrea and Ethiopia. Both states deny the charges.
Rebels said they launched the attack to put pressure on the Sudanese government and bring about a popular uprising.
Diplomats said Khaddam and Shara discussed Sudan with Egyptian leaders in Cairo on Friday. Syria maintains good ties with Sudan and Egypt.
The Sudanese opposition says it has seized several towns and garrisons in the Blue Nile area but the government only admits to the loss of Kurmuk and Qeissan near the Ethiopian border.
The rebels say their goal is to advance on Damazin, site of a hydroelectricity plant which supplies Khartoum with most its power.
